title: Mode FM under Band CB not selectable
body:
Hello,

I got another issue.

Under Band CB I'm not able to select Mode FM on my device.

I'd installed V1.09 with rotated display.
author: BrightCGN

Regards, Steffen

title: v1.08 FM Tuning
body: VHF FM tuning seems to no longer work for me with v1.08.
author: MattMan76

comments.body: Do you mean autotuning (press + rotate), or manual tuning? Also, how "does not work" actually manifests itself? Ideally, a demo video would be helpful

Actually, this can be closed, I just tested it again. My issue was just with the USB cable plugged in after updating I could no longer pick up FM signal.  So, it was just user error with the cable grounding it out or something. Sorry about that.

title: Setting/Volume UI bug
body:
Hi Max,
I noticed a minor bug in the UI.
Whilst in menu parameter setting, on middle press of the encoder (Volume shortcut), the volume adjustment pops up, but the adjustment is still setting the parameter that was active and the current volume is also painted.

Again, another one of these strange corner cases.
73, Dave
author: G8PTN

comments.body: I literally just came across this ten minutes ago when I was in settings/calibration, and needed to increase the volume. It's just a minor thing, but something to look into.

title: Faster tuning
body:
* Get rid of the delays and extra screen repaints
* Refactor the main loop a bit, fix some issues
author: max-arnold

comments.body: @G8PTN Could you please take a look? I worry whether this PR introduces some negative effects

Hi Max,
I am not sure if the assignment is essential, it may be redundant or a hang up from the original sources. In general reading from the SI4732 just makes sure that everything is aligned with the hardware.

There may be additional screen prints, which again may be a hang up from the original source, or I added them to ensure that the screen is updated after particular actions. I tried to make sure that the RSSI readings were updated whilst adjusting parameters, to provide some user feedback of changes as they were made.

With respect to all changes, you just need to thoroughly test everything to make sure that it works as expected. I did not try to make any code optimisations, since there was no intension to release the code, and it was only for personal use.

Time permitting, I would try to do a 100% code review and attempt to write some sort of automated test script to test everything in a controlled and methodical manner.

I am sure there will still be bugs in the code, like the LW/MW step limit, I missed it because I only tested the first MW band and it happened to work as expected, but the other bands would have failed.

73, Dave
